name: Inversion of Control in Spring
overview: Let Spring assemble the parts while your service does its job. Replace one dependency without editing the class that uses it.

sections.title: Give the container the wiring
sections.content: Inversion of Control means the container takes responsibility for creating and connecting managed objects. The service can focus on the work it was written to do.

images.caption: The container assembles dependencies so the service can focus on its work.

sections.title: Declare what the service needs
sections.content: Dependency injection supplies collaborators from outside. A constructor makes required dependencies visible and lets tests supply simpler substitutes.

sections.title: Make one change to prove it
sections.content: Wire a real repository into a service and a fake into a unit test. If the service works with both without changing its implementation, the dependency is genuinely replaceable.

codeExamples.title: ✅ Loosely Coupled Code

keyPoints: Wire a repository into a service, then swap in a fake. If the service stays unchanged, you've demonstrated IoC with DI.

interviewQA.question: How do IoC and DI relate?
interviewQA.answer: IoC is the broader transfer of control. Dependency injection is how the container supplies collaborators.

interviewQA.question: What is a Spring bean?
interviewQA.answer: An object created or otherwise managed by the Spring container.
